# Ask Alexa+ to Read Your Calendar Aloud and Get a Heads-Up Before Meetings

> **In short:** Link a Google or Microsoft calendar to Alexa in the Alexa app, then ask any Echo "what's on my calendar today?" to hear your meetings read out loud. Add a "remind me 10 minutes before my next meeting" command and Alexa+ will warn you ahead of each one.

Say one short sentence to your Echo in the morning and you'll hear today's meetings read out — with times, titles, and any details you've saved in the event itself. No phone, no typing, no scrolling. This guide walks a complete beginner through linking a calendar, picking the right voice command, and setting automatic reminders before each meeting.

## Before you start
- An Echo device (Echo Dot, Echo Show, or similar) or the Alexa app on a phone.
- A free Amazon account, signed in on both the device and the app.
- A Google or Microsoft calendar that already has at least one event on it.
- An Alexa+ subscription. Pricing, bundled offers and availability change often and differ by country — check Amazon's site in your region for the latest. In the US, Alexa+ is included with Prime, and separate plan options may also be available. Basic calendar reading on Echo devices works without Alexa+, but the smoother conversational replies described here are the Alexa+ experience.
- About 5–10 minutes for the first-time setup, then roughly 10 seconds per morning.

## Step 1 — Link your calendar to Alexa

Open the Alexa app on your phone and tap the **More** tab in the bottom-right corner, then choose **Settings**. Scroll until you see **Calendar** — if it isn't visible right away, try looking under "Account settings" or "Connected services" first. Tap your calendar provider (Google or Microsoft) and sign in with the same account that holds your events. A screen will ask if you want to give Alexa access; tap **Allow**. If your account has several calendars, pick the one you want Alexa+ to read from.

💬 Example: When asked "Which calendar should Alexa use?" choose "Work" if that's where your meetings live — not the "Holidays" or "Family" one.

If "Calendar" doesn't appear in the menu, tap the magnifying-glass search at the top of Settings and type "calendar" — it usually shows up immediately.

You'll know it worked when the app shows a checkmark or "Linked" label next to your account, and a recent event appears in the Calendar section.

## Step 2 — Make sure your Echo is awake and listening

Place your Echo somewhere you'll be in the morning — kitchen counter, bedside table, or desk. The light ring around the top should be **off** or glowing soft **blue**; that means Alexa is ready but not yet talking. If the ring is **red**, the microphone is muted — press the small microphone button on top once to unmute. If you don't own an Echo, open the Alexa app and tap the blue Alexa button at the bottom of the screen; it listens through your phone's mic.

💬 Example: Say *"Alexa, hello"* as a quick test. You should hear a short chime and a friendly spoken reply.

On devices with a screen (Echo Show), a thin blue light bar along the bottom edge does the same job the top ring does on a regular Echo.

You'll know it worked when Alexa answers your test question out loud — that confirms the microphone, speakers, and account are all wired up correctly.

## Step 3 — Ask Alexa+ to read today's meetings

Say clearly: *"Alexa, what's on my calendar today?"* A short chime plays, then Alexa+ starts reading each event in order — the time, the event title, and any details you've saved inside the entry (a location, a video-call link, an agenda note). Exactly which details are spoken back depends on what you put into the event itself. If today is empty, Alexa+ will say something like "You have no events scheduled for today."

💬 Example: *"Alexa, what are my meetings today?"* and *"Alexa, read my schedule"* work just as well. *"Alexa, what's next on my schedule?"* gives you only the very next event.

If Alexa+ answers with "I can't access your calendar" or "Please link a calendar first," go back to Step 1 — the link didn't take. Try unlinking and re-linking the account once.

You'll know it worked when you hear your real meetings read out loud, in the right order, with the correct times.

## Step 4 — Ask Alexa+ to remind you before each meeting

Now add the warning ahead of time. Say *"Alexa, remind me 10 minutes before my next meeting."* Alexa+ creates a reminder tied to your next calendar event. You can pick any lead time — 5 minutes, 15 minutes, even an hour. When the moment arrives, the Echo chimes and announces the meeting name. For back-to-back meetings, Alexa+ keeps tracking the next one automatically.

💬 Example: *"Alexa, remind me 10 minutes before my next meeting"* — Alexa+ confirms with "Okay, I'll remind you 10 minutes before [meeting name]."

If you only want a reminder for one specific meeting, say *"Alexa, remind me 15 minutes before my call with Maria"* and it will only fire for that one event.

You'll know it worked when Alexa+ repeats the meeting name and the lead time back to you as confirmation.

## Step 5 — Build your 10-second morning command

Pick one phrase and use it every day. The shorter and clearer the command, the more reliably Alexa+ understands it. A good all-in-one prompt: *"Alexa, good morning — what's on my calendar and remind me 10 minutes before each meeting."* That single sentence triggers both the schedule read-out and the day's reminders.

💬 Example: *"Alexa, good morning, what's on my calendar today and remind me 15 minutes before each meeting."* — a complete, copy-and-paste morning command.

If you'd rather split it, ask *"Alexa, what's my day look like?"* first, then set the reminder separately. Both approaches work the same.

You'll know it worked when Alexa+ reads your day and confirms the reminder in one go — you can keep getting ready while it talks.

## Common mistakes
- **Skipping the calendar link.** The most common reason "Alexa, what's on my calendar?" fails is that no calendar is linked yet. Open the Alexa app → More → Settings → Calendar and connect a Google or Microsoft account before you start asking.
- **Linked the wrong calendar.** If you have multiple Google calendars (work, personal, family, holidays), Alexa+ only reads the one you picked. Open the app, check the selected default, and switch it if needed.
- **Asking while the mic is muted.** A red light ring means Alexa cannot hear you. Press the microphone button on top once and wait for the ring to turn blue before you speak.
- **Expecting Alexa+ to change the calendar for you.** It can read events and set reminders, but it cannot move, edit, or cancel meetings on your behalf. Update the event in your calendar app; Alexa+ picks up the change within a couple of minutes.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** Say one sentence while brushing your teeth and hear the full day out loud — no screen, no scrolling, no notifications buried under twenty other apps. Handy for parents juggling school runs, drivers on the way to work, visually impaired users, or anyone who simply prefers listening.
- **For your work or business:** Use it to never walk into a meeting unprepared. A 10-minute warning gives you time to find the link, open the right tab, and skim the agenda. Teams running back-to-back calls lose several minutes a day to "wait, what's next?" — this removes that.
- **If you're just getting started:** Don't try to set reminders for every meeting at once. Link the calendar, ask once, and only add a reminder if you actually need it. Small steps beat over-engineering.

## Try it now
Open the Alexa app, link your Google or Microsoft calendar, then walk up to any Echo in your home and say: *"Alexa, what's on my calendar today?"* — that's the whole first move. If it works, add one reminder tomorrow: *"Alexa, remind me 10 minutes before my next meeting."*
